speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where your wrist pain is located, when it started, and describe the skin lesions you mentioned?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any circular, expanding red rashes on your skin during or after your camping trip in Minnesota? Have you observed any heart rhythm abnormalities or facial drooping recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those violaceous lesions on your hands and wrists are a very specific sign, especially given your recent exposure in Minnesota. REQUEST TEST: Tick_Borne_Disease_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal tick-borne panel is a significant clue, especially given the classic "bull's-eye" or violaceous lesions and the migratory arthritis pattern. This presentation strongly suggests Acute Rheumatic Fever rather than Lyme disease. REQUEST TEST: Anti-Streptolysin_O_Titer

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal tick-borne and strep panels rule out the most common causes, but the violaceous lesions and migratory arthritis are highly specific for Erythema Chronicum Migrans variants or other spirochetal infections. REQUEST TEST: Lyme_EIA_and_Western_Blot

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative Lyme and strep tests are unexpected given the classic Minnesota exposure and violaceous lesions, so I must consider alternative diagnoses like Hand-Foot-and-Mouth Disease or a viral arthritis. Let me examine the lesions more closely to check for oral involvement or other systemic signs. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the sexual history and diaphragm use, I need to rule out sexually transmitted infections that can cause reactive arthritis or disseminated gonococcal infection. REQUEST TEST: Gonococcus_and_Chlamydia_PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Gonorrhea test confirms Disseminated Gonococcal Infection, which aligns perfectly with the migratory arthritis and characteristic pustular skin lesions. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
